description:
A harness mode that times zero-mask detection plus the complete nonzero horizontal reduction, reporting the fast and slow paths separately.

## Background

The study must isolate three nested measurement shapes for each arithmetic representation it measures: one dependency-chained packed add or subtract on the same accumulator; zero-mask detection plus the complete nonzero horizontal reduction; and the full Ryser loop including matrix preparation, Gray initialization, update, product, partial-sum reduction, launch overhead, and transfer overhead. The harness times the third shape and, through its per-phase event columns, separates the device spans inside it. The first two shapes have no measurement path at all.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Gray update micro-measurement] --> B[Horizontal product micro-measurement]
    B --> C[End-to-end Ryser cell]
    C --> D[Per-phase device spans inside the cell]
```

This matters because a representation decision made on bulk independent-operator throughput does not transfer to the permanent: the shipped row-packed loop performs one packed add or subtract per Gray step followed by a horizontal product over the row lanes, and it is the dependency chain through the accumulator that a permanent-shaped measurement has to expose.

This mode covers the second shape. Its defining property is the branch: the horizontal product exits early when any active row sum is zero and runs the full reduction otherwise, and the two paths have different costs and different frequencies, so a single blended figure hides the quantity the representation comparison turns on.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A harness mode times zero-mask detection plus the complete nonzero horizontal reduction for a measured path.
- [hard] REQ-02: The mode reports the zero fast path and the nonzero slow path separately where the measured path permits the distinction, and states the reason where it does not.
- [hard] REQ-03: The mode reports the observed frequency of each path beside its exact marginal expectation, the zero fast path against $1 - \left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n$ and the nonzero slow path against $\left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n$, noting that the two are complements.
- [hard] REQ-04: The mode reuses the committed warm-up, repetition-count, timed-duration, and censoring policy of the harness protocol module instead of defining a private timing policy, and a censored row states its censoring reason.
- [hard] REQ-05: For a GPU path the mode reports an event-measured kernel duration rather than a wall-clock span.
- [hard] REQ-06: The mode addresses the sampler through a named purpose tag drawn from the harness's enumerated purpose set, with no numeric stream base computed in the mode's own code.
- [hard] REQ-07: The mode reaches candidates through the harness's registry-derived schedule, so it covers a registered path without a schedule edit.
- [hard] REQ-08: The harness usage text describes the mode together with its arguments.
- [hard] REQ-09: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/Cargo.toml --release` passes.

## Notes

Scope is this one mode. With it the harness covers all three nested measurement shapes the study needs, and no campaign receipt is produced here.

Every crate under `dev/research/` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles them; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.
title: Horizontal product micro-measurement mode
